packets.signature: EASE_INFLUENCE_MARGIN = 0.02 (module-scoped const, motion.js:11709); easeOutPercent(k) -> number|null (0-100, rounded; null if k.curvePoints is falsy or has <2 points); easeInPercent(k) -> number|null (same contract, mirrored end); editableInfluenceCurve(key) -> curvePoints array (always length>=5 on return); setSegmentInfluence(key, side:'in'|'out', percent:number) -> boolean (false only if key is falsy; true otherwise, unconditionally); keyEaseInfluence(holder, prop, key, side) -> number|null; setSelectedEaseInfluence(side, value) -> number (count of segments actually changed, 0 if _motionKeySel is empty or no selected key owns that side's segment); isPrimarySelectedKey(holder, prop, key) -> boolean.
packets.responsibility: Lead-in (11683-11691, MISPLACED — see boundaries) documents subdivideKeys (declared 169 lines later at 11860), not the influence model that follows it. Influence lead-in (11692-11708, 2026-08 rework) frames the semantic flip explicitly quoted from feedback: previously percent only varied a waypoint's Y at a FIXED x=0.25 (0%/100% meant 'linear' vs 'fully held' but the waypoint never moved in time); now percent drives the waypoint's X too — 0% keeps it hugging its OWN key's time (negligible reach), 100% pushes it toward the segment's fixed midpoint at x=0.5 (11703-11705, 'the on-curve waypoint model used everywhere here... has a fixed midpoint at x=0.5 that the out-side waypoint can approach but never cross, and the in-side mirrors it from the other end'). EASE_INFLUENCE_MARGIN=0.02 (11709) keeps a waypoint strictly short of coinciding with x=0 (or x=1) OR with the fixed x=0.5 midpoint, since a zero-width span would degenerate curveSegFor's own segment lookup (11706-11708, cited by name only, not called from this span). easeOutPercent(k) (11710-11717): reads `pts=k.curvePoints`; null if pts has fewer than 2 points; else `p=pts[1]` (the waypoint immediately after the key's own point 0, i.e. the OUT-side waypoint of the OUTGOING segment); `amount=(p.x-MARGIN)/(0.5-2*MARGIN)` maps p.x's clamped range [MARGIN, 0.5-MARGIN] back onto [0,1], then rounds `clamp(amount,0,1)*100` to an integer percent. easeInPercent(k) (11718-11725): mirrors it from the other end — `p=pts[pts.length-2]` (second-to-last waypoint, the IN-side waypoint of the segment this same key's curvePoints array describes) and `amount=(1-p.x-MARGIN)/(0.5-2*MARGIN)`, same rounding. Both are pure reads; neither mutates `k`. editableInfluenceCurve(key) (11726-11736): `cloneCurvePts(key.curvePoints||CURVE_LINEAR)` (CURVE_LINEAR, motion.js:957, C02, a 2-point array); if the cloned array has fewer than 4 points (true only for CURVE_LINEAR itself, since every other curve constant in this file — DEFAULT_CURVE motion.js:935, CURVE_EASE/CURVE_EASE_IN/CURVE_EASE_OUT motion.js:965/969-970 — is already 5 points), it is replaced by a literal 5-point array `[{0,0},{.25,.25},{.5,.5},{.75,.75},{1,1}]` — NOT DEFAULT_CURVE's own smoothstep values (cross-checked against DEFAULT_CURVE's actual value, src/js/domain/animation/opacity.js:7 = `[{0,0},{.25,.156},{.5,.5},{.75,.844},{1,1}]`; the two differ at x=0.25/0.75). This promotion therefore preserves LINEAR's exact identity shape (y=x at every waypoint) while giving each edge its own independently-movable waypoint, per the comment's own stated intent (11728-11730, 'while the untouched edge remains exactly linear') — it is not a promotion toward the ease-in-out default. setSegmentInfluence(key, side, percent) (11737-11762), the EXACT INVERSE of easeOutPercent/easeInPercent: `amount=clamp(percent,0,100)/100`; `reach=MARGIN+amount*(0.5-2*MARGIN)` (the same x-value easeOutPercent/easeInPercent would decode back to `amount`); `pts=editableInfluenceCurve(key)` (promotes/clones first, so the source key object is never mutated in place before this line). If side==='out': `p=pts[1]`; `p.x=reach`; `p.y=p.x*(1-amount)` (11749, deepens toward y=0 as amount/reach grow — 'hold near this key, then catch up'). Else (side==='in'): `p=pts[pts.length-2]`; `p.x=1-reach` (mirrored position); `p.y=1-(1-p.x)*(1-amount)` (mirrored deepening toward y=1). Either branch then `delete p.tx; delete p.ty` (11758, releases any hand-dragged tangent on ONLY that one waypoint — every other point in `pts`, including the untouched x=0.5 midpoint and the opposite edge's waypoint, is left byte-for-byte as `editableInfluenceCurve` produced it); `key.hold=false` (an influence edit always clears hold-interpolation on that key); `key.curvePoints=pts` (11761, the actual document write — the ONLY place in this artifact that writes `key.curvePoints`); returns true. keyEaseInfluence(holder, prop, key, side) (11763-11770) answers 'which key does a side belong to': `track=trackFor(holder,prop)` (motion.js:443, C02); `idx=track.keys.indexOf(key)`; if side==='out', returns `easeOutPercent(key)` directly (key's OWN out-side waypoint) but ONLY if `idx>=0 && idx<track.keys.length-1` (key is not the last — an outgoing segment exists), else null. If side==='in', it does NOT read `key.curvePoints` at all — it looks at `prev=idx>0?track.keys[idx-1]:null` (the PREVIOUS key) and returns `easeInPercent(prev)`, because a segment's curvePoints live on its LEFT (earlier) endpoint key (confirmed at motion.js:964, 'A key's curvePoints govern the segment LEAVING it (valueAtFrame reads the left key's curve)', pre-1683/C02) — so the in-side box drawn NEXT TO key i actually reads and later writes key (i-1)'s own curvePoints[pts.length-2], never key i's. In short: for the segment between key i and key i+1, BOTH its out-side (from key i's perspective) and in-side (from key i+1's perspective) waypoints live in the SAME curvePoints array, owned by key i (the left/earlier key of that segment) — 'side' names which end of THAT one array a caller wants, not which key object the caller passed when asking for 'in'. setSelectedEaseInfluence(side, value) (11771-11789): returns 0 immediately if `_motionKeySel` (motion.js:11388, sibling-covered) is empty (no pushUndo in that case). Otherwise calls `pushUndo()` (tweens.js:4741) UNCONDITIONALLY before the loop, then iterates EVERY selected key `s` in `_motionKeySel` (not just the primary one — see isPrimarySelectedKey below, which governs UI display, not this function's own scope): for each, re-derives which key object actually owns the requested side's segment using the SAME idx/side logic as keyEaseInfluence (side==='out': the key itself if it is not the last on its track; side==='in': the previous key on its track, if any) and, if such a segment exists, calls `setSegmentInfluence(segment, side, value)`, incrementing `n` on success. After the loop, if `n` is nonzero: `renderLayerList()` (timeline.js:6335), `renderTimeline()` (timeline.js:4026), and `window.SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` if the engine bridge global exists — a live repaint. Returns `n`. Net effect: applying an influence percent to a MULTI-key selection changes every selected key's OWN matching-side segment independently (each key's neighbor may differ), not just a single 'primary' key's segment. isPrimarySelectedKey(holder, prop, key) (11790-11800): false immediately if the key is not itself selected (via `isKeySelected`, motion.js:11412, C20o). If a `_keyAnchor` (motion.js:11411, sibling-covered) exists AND the anchor is STILL present in the current `_motionKeySel` (an anchor can go stale after e.g. a subdivide/invert reshuffles the array), the primary key is defined as whichever key exactly matches the anchor's own holder/prop/frame — i.e. the anchor IS the primary while it remains selected. Otherwise (no anchor, or the anchor fell out of the current selection), the primary is simply the LAST entry of `_motionKeySel` (the most recently added/re-ordered selection item). This is a pure predicate — no document or selection write.
